Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 25-Nov-2024 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. (COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING) EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER / DECEMBER 2024  
  SUBJECT: CSE 2121/CSE_2121 - COMPUTER ORGANIZATION & ARCHITECTURE  
  COMPUTER ORGANIZATION and ARCHITECTURE [CSE 2121]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               In a robotics lab, a CISC-based processor is programmed to calculate the dot product of two sensor (5)  
  data arrays, SENSOR_A and SENSOR_B, each with N elements. The program loads the base  
  addresses of both arrays, then loops through each element pair, multiplying them, adding the  
  product to a register, and decrementing a counter COUNT until all elements are processed. The  
  result is stored in DOT_PRODUCT of memory. Describe the sequence of operations required  
  through suitable codes and explanations.  
1B)               Convert the decimal numbers 15.75 and 42.5 into IEEE 754 single-precision format. Perform the          (3)  
  addition of these two numbers using their IEEE 754 representations and analyse the process to  
  ensure accuracy. Write the result of the addition in both IEEE 754 single-precision format and  
  decimal format.  
1C)               Represent the following integers in 2's complement representation with minimum number of bits          (2)  
  required, perform the operation mentioned and state whether overflow occurs or not in each case.  
  Also, if overflow has occurred, state why it has occurred:  
  (a) Add -13 and 12  
  (b) Subtract -7 and 6  
2A)               Perform the Booth's multiplication algorithm to multiply -12 and -11. Show the sequence of steps       (3)  
  clearly and indicate the result. Use minimum number of bits required.  
2B)               Design a flowchart to illustrate the step-by-step process of restoring division method in detail.      (2)  
2C)               Consider the Register Transfer description given below. Draw a neat, microprogrammed control         (5)  
  unit. Analyze and Explain your design with the help of the contents of condition-select field and  
  actions taken. Write the binary listing of the microprogram for the microprogrammed control unit you  
  designed.  
  
  
  Page 1 of 2

3A)   Compare and list the pros and cons of both hardwired and microprogrammed control unit.                   (2)  
3B)   Elaborate the working of virtual memory and address translation in detail.                               (5)  
3C)   A processing section uses three registers X, Y and Z each of with 4-bit in size. It uses Inbus and       (3)  
  Outbus each of them being 4-lines. Register X must be loaded with Inbus, Register Y is cleared to 0  
  and counter Register Z is loaded with 9. It is required to add the X and Y Register contents  
  iteratively. Store the sum in Register Y after each iteration. For each iteration the counter register Z  
  is decremented. This process of adding X and Y register contents and storing the sum in Register Y  
  is to be done till the counter register Z becomes 0. Transfer the final sum stored in Register Y to the  
  Outbus. Write a register transfer description algorithm to meet the above.  
4A)   Design a memory chip to show the organization a memory of 2G × 16 memory module using 256K               (3)  
  × 8 static memory chips.  
4B)   Explain how data is organized and accessed in a disk assembly. Consider a long sequence of          (5)  
  accesses to a disk with an average seek time of 10 ms and an average rotational delay of 6 ms.  
  The average size of a block being accessed is 16K bytes. The data transfer rate from the disk is 24  
  Mbytes/sec. Assuming that the data blocks are randomly located on the disk, estimate the average  
  percentage of the total time occupied by seek operations and rotational delays.  
4C)   Contrast between bandwidth and effective throughput of an interconnection network. Justify the           (2)  
  need for arbitration when bus interconnection network is employed in a shared-memory  
  multiprocessing architecture.  
5A)   Define an interrupt. What is its advantage over program controlled I/O? Illustrate (with a neat          (5)  
  diagram) how an interrupt request from an I/O device is handled by the processor.  
5B)   Define bandwidth of an interconnection network. Briefly describe the features and limitations of bus (3)  
  and ring-based interconnection network.  
5C)   Consider the below RISC code snippet:                                                                    (2)  
  
  
  Identify the type of data dependency between the two instructions. How can the operand forwarding  
  technique overcome this issue?
